paragraphs.text: The National Weather Service now puts the chance of Sunday rain in Pontotoc County near 100%, up from 70% in Wednesday’s forecast. For travelers heading home after Thanksgiving, the Friday update narrows the wettest part of the weekend to early Sunday. Saturday still looks sunny, with a high in the mid-60s.

The first showers are likely after midnight Saturday night. The forecast for the city of Pontotoc places their likely arrival after 4 a.m. Sunday. Across the county, the overnight rain chance has doubled from 30% to 60%. South winds could gust to 25 mph before daybreak.

Sunday morning brings a slight chance of thunderstorms along with the showers. By afternoon, forecasters expect some sun and a chance of lingering showers. The day’s high should reach the mid-60s, but the temperature is expected to fall into the mid-50s during the afternoon as winds of 15 to 20 mph turn from south to west.

Forecasters in Memphis expect the cold front to bring an average of less than two-tenths of an inch of rain across the region. They put the likelihood of strong or severe thunderstorms low because the air ahead of the front is expected to be only weakly unstable. Sunday night in Pontotoc County should turn mostly clear and much colder, with lows in the lower 30s. Monday’s forecast calls for sunshine and a high in the mid-50s.
